_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform. `quick-xml` reads AND writes real XML 1.0 documents, so it is registered here under a distinct id and the `xml-1-0-mutate` capability this subset's exhaustive mutation case (`mutate-xml-1-0`) actually tags, per the wave 7 fleet brief's oracle-registration gotcha (reusing a neighbour's entry fails the contract with `oracle-capability-mismatch`).

oracles.rationale: The reference streaming XML reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem, and the only registered crate that both parses and re-serializes XML, so it can independently produce a second result for every one of this subset's 8 `XmlMutation` kinds rather than merely reading. Registered under its own id/capability so this subset's catalog is measured against a reference surveyed for exactly this vocabulary.

comparisonProfiles.description: XML 1.0 documents compared by declaration, doctype, prolog and the full element tree in document order. Attribute order is writer freedom -- each element's attributes project as an unordered name/value map rather than an ordered list. Self-closing vs paired empty-element form is invisible once decoded (both denote the same zero-children element) and numeric vs named character/entity references are invisible once decoded (both resolve to the same literal text), so neither needs an ignored key. Sibling and child order IS normative and is never sorted.
